? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 09:07:35 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.80)
events.body:
The complaint concerns one off-route stretch: 09:07–09:14, 4.13 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, adding 2.36 km and reaching up to 1304 m off the optimal route [F3]. RD-1 makes each such segment reviewable, and the trace confirms one unexempted segment exists [F3][RD-1]. The passenger's own case is that the fare is fixed, and the fare record agrees: distance is billed at exactly the optimal 16.5 km (16.53 km) with no excess [F4][F6].

Applying RD-2: RydeX is a non-metered service whose fare is a one-off quote and does not vary with distance, so the detour kilometres do not enter the fare; only ERP/toll or post-trip unpublished add-ons could be refundable [F6][RD-2]. No toll/ERP item appears in the charged breakdown (base $3.90 + distance $23.31 + time $5.64 + platform $1.47 = $34.32), so the refundable amount is $0 → no_action, with the RD-1 breach recorded [F6][F4][RD-2].

The driver's post-trip statement that his GPS rerouted him is a claim, not a reasonable-cause exemption: no traffic incident sits on the replaced optimal stretch before the detour, and speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) alone does not exempt [F10][F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. There is no rider consent on record either: the complete, fully timestamped two-message chat contains only pickup logistics and nothing agreeing to a route, so the F3 segment counts [F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. The F3 timing question changes neither amount (fixed fare, $0 refundable) nor account action (0 prior upheld route disputes, so RD-6 does not trigger), so an undetermined reading of consent would not alter this outcome [F4][F16][RD-2][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages (pickup meeting and vehicle description), the driver's statement and the rider's complaint [F7][F8][F10]. Nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving; no safety clause is engaged.

Evidence is sufficient: the GPS segment, fare breakdown and complete timestamped chat settle every element this ruling turns on [F3][F4][F6][F9]; no gap remains. Rejected claims follow.

notices.text: We have reviewed your dispute: the charge stands. The decision follows Ryde's dispute policy and the trip record.

Nothing is deducted from you and no voucher applies here. Keep driving as usual.
